newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to use morality to enfore new rich tax.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to use morality to enfore new rich tax.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto has said big businesses that failed to pay a two percent levy on their after-tax incomes would be "morally chastised", the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Monday.

The levy, contained in a presidential decree signed earlier this month and released last week, applies to companies and individuals with an after-tax income of more than 100 million rupiah ($42,000). It will be given to a foundation to help the poor.
The decree did not prescribe penalties for those who failed to pay the tax order, although it was a revision of a 1995 decree which had made the donations voluntary.

"In this country, according to (the state ideology) Pancasila, those who are able should be willing to help the weak," Suharto said speaking to villagers in Central Java on Sunday during a Women's Day ceremony.
"Just mark those business people who refuse to donate two percent of their profits to help the poor," Suharto said.
"There's no need to lash out or be upset. Just mark their houses...with flags or whatever, they should be ashamed then," he was quoted as saying.
Suharto slammed business people last September when he revealed only about half of the 11,000 eligible taxpayers had complied with his earlier request.

The taxpayers must pay their contribution directly to Yayasan Dana Sejahtera Mandiri (The Self Relient Welfare Fund Foundation) which is run by senior government figures, including the director-general of taxation.
